adjustments.tool: this app (built-in trail detection and repair)
adjustments.note: Whether to detect and remove a satellite/aircraft trail (a long thin straight bright line) before processing.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Wrongly on: a real linear feature (e.g. a diffraction spike) gets painted over. Wrongly off: a bright streak crosses the finished image.

adjustments.note: Fraction of the frame trimmed from each edge to remove the ragged stacking border.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too low: dark ragged edges survive into the finished image and skew the background model. Too high: you lose usable sky area.

adjustments.note: How smooth the modeled light-pollution gradient is before it is subtracted.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too low: the model chases real nebulosity and eats faint structure. Too high: strong local gradients survive subtraction.

adjustments.note: How much AI noise smoothing is applied (0.0–1.0). Counter-intuitively, more denoise reveals MORE faint stars (they rise above the detection threshold). Values around 0.6 are typical; faint galaxies use about 0.65, while dense stellar cores (clusters) can begin to over-smooth above roughly 0.6–0.7.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: creamy/plastic look, dense star cores smear together. Too low: grainy background, faint stars missing.

adjustments.note: Whether photometric color calibration (PCC) runs. The app decides from the filter and measured category: dual-band LP filters and star clusters keep native color; broadband galaxies get calibrated.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Wrongly on (dual-band nebula): deep red emission washes to pink. Wrongly off (broadband galaxy): the body keeps an uncalibrated color cast.

adjustments.note: Color saturation applied after the stretch (threshold 0, so faint signal is saturated too).
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: neon color, hues pinned to the rail (the QA pegged-chroma gate fails). Too low: gray, lifeless image.

adjustments.note: The asinh stretch depth — the contrast SHAPE of the lift (the brightness LEVEL is solved separately per image).
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: the faint field lifts into visible noise and bright cores flatten. Too low: the subject looks small, dim and underwhelming.

adjustments.tool: this app (per-image solver) — applied via Siril's midtone lift
adjustments.note: The output level the stretch solver aims for (0–255 scale): extended targets solve the subject's brightness (body p90), star fields solve the sky median. This is THE brightness knob.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: gray washed-out sky, blown cores. Too low: dark, small-looking subject that does not fill the frame.

adjustments.note: Whether the measured structure treatment (GHS) runs on top of the base stretch — nebula envelope, galaxy dust lane, or cluster halo. Pinning this true can only UN-DO an 'off' decision the profile or preferences made — it cannot invent a structure treatment for an image the engine decided has none.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Wrongly on: overcooked look on weak data. Wrongly off: the faint envelope/halo/dust lane the data supports stays invisible.

adjustments.note: How strongly stars are blended back into the star-reduced hero image (screen blend strength k).
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: the star field competes with the subject. Too low: an eerie, nearly starless sky that reads as fake.

adjustments.tool: this app (measured from the image) — applied via Siril's asinh stretch
adjustments.note: The stretch black point, set just BELOW the measured sky level so the background is dark but the faint star field survives. The app re-computes this from the image each run; leave your_value null unless you want to force it.
adjustments.reason: measured: factor 0.987 x linear sky median 0.018409; raised by the two-point sky solve to hold the sky at 17.2
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too high: faint stars vanish and the frame looks empty (a black point above the sky median once cut a star field from ~900 stars to 26). Too low: gray, washed-out background.

adjustments.tool: this app (per-image solver) — applied via Siril's midtone lift
adjustments.note: The midtone lift applied after asinh. The app solves this per image so the render hits brightness_target. The app re-computes this from the image each run; leave your_value null unless you want to force it.
adjustments.symptoms_if_wrong: Too low: washed-out gray sky. Too high: dim, flat subject. If brightness is what you want to change, pin brightness_target instead — it survives re-solves.
